events.title: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa Drowns on the Third Crusade
events.description: While leading a large German army toward Jerusalem, Holy Roman Emperor Frederick I drowned in the River Saleph in Anatolia. He was one of the most powerful rulers in Europe.
events.significance: His death left the Crusader army leaderless. Much of it turned back, which weakened the German contribution to the Third Crusade.

events.title: First Execution of the Salem Witch Trials
events.description: Bridget Bishop was hanged in Salem, Massachusetts, after being convicted of witchcraft. She was the first person executed during the trials.
events.significance: Her hanging began a wave of executions in colonial New England. It has become a lasting warning about mass hysteria and unfair trials.

events.title: Birth of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
events.description: Prince Philip was born into the Greek and Danish royal families. He later became the husband of Queen Elizabeth II.
events.significance: He was the longest-serving royal consort in British history. He supported the monarchy for decades and founded the Duke of Edinburgh's Award for young people.

events.title: Alcoholics Anonymous Is Founded
events.description: Bill Wilson and Dr. Bob Smith founded the mutual-aid fellowship in Akron, Ohio, to help people overcome alcoholism through peer support.
events.significance: Alcoholics Anonymous grew into a worldwide organization. Its twelve-step approach has shaped many other recovery programs.

events.title: Italy Declares War on France and Britain
events.description: Benito Mussolini announced that Italy would enter World War II on the side of Nazi Germany. This came as German forces were sweeping through France.
events.significance: Italy's entry widened the war to the Mediterranean and North Africa. It also tied Italy's fate to that of the Axis powers.
